Beam Physics Manual

Symplectic modelling of a magnetic storage ring with an RF cavity. The independent variable is the arc length $s$ along the reference orbit. All dynamics are written in canonical phase-space variables; laboratory angles and RF phase appear only as derived output.

The object of the ring is a product of Lie transformations, not a stack of transport matrices and not a truncated Taylor map. Each element has one Hamiltonian. That $H$ becomes a Dragt–Finn factor $R\circ e^{:f_3:}\circ e^{:f_4:}$. Concatenation in the algebra produces the one-turn factor $\mathcal{F}$. Twiss, slip, chromaticity and the normal form are readings of $\mathcal{F}$. Tracking applies $\mathcal{F}$ to a point. An RK4 polynomial map is kept as a check; it does not define the ring.

Linear optics, second-order slip and chromaticity are homogeneous pieces of the same polynomial, not layers derived from one another.

Figures use the Nuclotron-based lattice at deuteron kinetic energy 270 MeV unless a ramp from 10 MeV is shown. A separate Programmer Manual documents the implementation.
